minor.issue: OBSERVED ONCE, THEN NOT REPRODUCIBLE. On the first run, a rich-brief one-shot call returned Cloudflare 502 Bad Gateway (edge timeout ~100s) because Haiku answered slowly and both attempts inside auto_build_from_brief plus its outer retry stacked to >100s wall time (35s attempt-1 timeout + 20s attempt-2 + 1.5s sleep, then the OUTER _call retry doubles that per parallel branch). Backend itself did NOT raise an unhandled exception — logs show the LLM calls eventually completed at 16:34:57 and the response was ready by ~16:35:20, well after Cloudflare had already returned 502 to the client. On a fresh run 3 minutes later the same request completed in 34s → 200. This is a latency-vs-edge-timeout tail-risk, not a bug. Recommended tightening (see action_items): reduce STEP_TIMEOUT_S/STEP_RETRY_TIMEOUT_S OR drop the inner _call retry inside auto_build_from_brief (_run already retries once — the extra outer retry in _call is what pushes worst-case wall time past 100s). Reproducing this reliably would require load-testing against a slow Anthropic day.

All 10 returned 200 (well below ThreadPoolExecutor+Semaphore saturation threshold). No 5xx, no dropped connections. If a 503 had come, it would carry Retry-After per contract — assertion covers that branch too.

action_items: OPTIONAL (tail-latency hardening — not blocking): in ai_engine.py::auto_build_from_brief, the inner _call has its own retry loop AROUND _run, and _run itself already retries once (STEP_TIMEOUT_S=35s → STEP_RETRY_TIMEOUT_S=20s + 1.5s sleep). Worst case wall time per branch is therefore 35+1.5+20 = 56.5s (attempt 1 of _run), then _call sees failure and calls _run again → another 56.5s = 113s. asyncio.gather(A,B) runs both branches in parallel, but the SLOWER branch drives wall time — so the whole /projects/{id}/situation call can exceed Cloudflare's ~100s edge timeout on a slow Anthropic day. Recommend: EITHER (a) drop the outer _call retry (rely on _run's built-in retry) so worst case is ~57s per branch; OR (b) trim STEP_RETRY_TIMEOUT_S from 20s to 12s so worst case (57s inner + 57s outer, but each branch capped shorter) stays below 100s. This surfaced once in this iteration as a Cloudflare 502; the second run 3min later completed in 34s. Currently below the reproducibility threshold to fail a test — flagged for E1 review.

OPTIONAL (test-user email domain): Resend rejects any address ending in @example.com and the backend logs a full traceback each time (though it recovers via console fallback). If you want cleaner backend.err.log during automated runs, either add @example.com to a 'skip Resend' whitelist in auth.py::send_otp_email, OR switch tests to Resend's testing address 'delivered@resend.dev'. Not a bug — just log noise. Confirmed non-fatal: /auth/otp/request still returns dev_code in body per OTP_TEST_MODE=1.
critical_code_review_comments: auto_build_from_brief has TWO nested retry loops (inner _call wraps _run; _run's own retry is 2 attempts). Worst case wall time = (attempt1 + attempt2 + backoff) * outer_attempts ≈ 113s per parallel branch — exceeds Cloudflare's ~100s edge timeout. Recommendation above.

server.py is 4334 lines — well beyond the 700-line threshold in the code-review guidelines. Splitting into route modules (auth, projects, steps, share, admin, exports) would materially help maintenance and reduce accidental route-ordering bugs (a class of bug the file's size makes hard to spot). Not a regression — flagging as tech debt.

share_status conflict semantics rely on string equality in /unlock and /reset-from-step (both correctly return 409 when share_status != 'none'). Verified working. Consider extracting a small helper `assert_not_shared_with_client(project)` to DRY the check across the two endpoints.

OTP fallback in /app/backend/auth.py logs a full Traceback (via logger.error+exc_info implicit) every time Resend rejects an @example.com domain. For automated test suites this is expected but noisy; a targeted `except resend.exceptions.ValidationError` branch that logs a single warning line would be cleaner.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is clean end-to-end: auth (OTP + password + guest), all 5 AI steps (situation/context/decision/artifacts/lock), share flow, exports (md+pdf), unlock/reset semantics (200 unshared, 409 shared), error hygiene (404 for bad ids, 422 for malformed bodies), and 10-concurrent /api/suggest all pass. The ONLY tail-latency risk is the one-shot auto-build path in step 1 with a very rich raw_paste on a slow-Anthropic day — the double retry stack can exceed Cloudflare's ~100s edge timeout and surface as a client-visible 502. This is documented in action_items[0]. To reproduce reliably you would need to add fault injection into ai_engine.py._run to force multiple 35s timeouts. Keeping current behaviour is acceptable if E1 decides — the frontend already retries 503 and the situation endpoint is safe to re-submit (framing-only path fires on the retry). rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bug fixes were required in application code. Two test-assertion typos on my side were fixed (auth/me returns the user object unwrapped, not under a 'user' key). One transient Cloudflare 502 on the initial one-shot rich-brief run was traced to compounded retry timeouts in ai_engine.auto_build_from_brief (inner _call retry + _run built-in retry), which under a slow Anthropic response can push wall time past ~100s and hit the CDN edge timeout. Second run of the same test in the same session completed cleanly in 34s → 200, confirming the code path is functionally correct and this is a latency ceiling issue, not a code correctness bug. Full RCA and remediation options captured in action_items[0].
